plan.title: Mouse tumor immune/stromal composition: anti-PD-1 vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 6-vs-6 unpaired mouse subcutaneous tumor bulk RNA-seq study (anti-PD-1 vs isotype control, Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples, single batch). The research question is about immune/stromal cell composition and its difference between treatment arms, which routes to the immune-profiling-agent using organism-appropriate deconvolution. Human deconvolution tools (MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq) are explicitly forbidden on mouse data per the knowledge base flag (R-0136): their marker sets and reference profiles are human-derived and not transferable. The tool of record, mMCP-counter, is present in this environment (R (GitHub) mMCPcounter==1.1.0) and is used as the primary quantitative estimate of 16 murine immune/stromal populations from linear-scale expression. As a complementary, method-independent check, UCell rank-based per-sample signature scores are computed from PanglaoDB mouse immune/stromal marker genes — flagged in the report as a relative-enrichment signature score, not a fraction, per R-0135/R-0133. Sample sample_01's ~4x-below-median library size is kept through QC, inspected on PCA/sample-distance plots, and its effect on both deconvolution and scoring is reported rather than silently dropped (R-0008/R-0030). Composition and signature-score differences between anti-PD-1 and isotype control are tested with two-group comparisons (Wilcoxon for the bounded mMCP-counter scores, given only n=6/6 and no distributional guarantee of normality, with BH correction across cell types) and with limma on the UCell scores (BH across signatures), per R-0134. A parallel gene-level DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage is run so that any composition shift found can be cross-checked against genes known to mark that cell type, and so that a compositional explanation for bulk DE signal is made explicit (R-0132) — composition is reported as a covariate/context for DE, not folded into its design, since the research question is about composition itself. The plan closes with an integrated report presenting composition per sample, per-group comparison, and its relation to the transcriptome-wide analysis.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.

Do not run a human deconvolution method on mouse data. The marker sets and the reference profiles of MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, and quanTIseq come from human samples, and a mouse symbol that maps to a human marker does not carry the same specificity in mouse tissue. The mouse tool of record is mMCP-counter, the mouse version of MCP-counter with markers from mouse data, and it is absent from this pool. Stop the deconvolution and ask for mMCP-counter or for a mouse reference, or give a descriptive signature score from mouse marker sets with the caution that it is not a deconvolution.
